# sheet-hyperobjects: full context for coding agents

> Last Updated: 2026-10-10
>
> Boundary checkpoint (2026-10-10): public repository. Operational detail (topology, secrets,
> runbooks, people) lives in MADFAM's private ops repository under the repo-boundary contract
> (docs/PUBLIC_REPO_BOUNDARY.md). Never copy it here.

## What this is

The commons of sheet hyperobjects. A sheet object's source is its **flat sheet** (outline, cuts,
creases — mountain, valley, score, perforation — and glue tabs) plus its **fold program**; every
3-D state is derived from them. The cartridge's generator (`main.py`) writes a sheet document
(FOLD 1.2 plus the `pliego:` namespace, the contract in Pliego's `docs/spec/v1/sheet-document.md`).
Pliego's engine animates it with the physics of a real paper stock (Pliego's `materials/*`).

## Cartridge contract

- Layout: `<slug>/main.py`, `<slug>/project.json`, `<slug>/docs/README.md`, at the repository root.
- Slugs: `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, 2–80 characters, permanent once landed.
- Manifest: validated by `pliego-spec check cartridge <slug>` from hyperobjects-spec at a pinned SHA.
- Licence: `project.attribution.license` == `hyperobject.commons_license` == `CERN-OHL-W-2.0`
  (owner ruling, 2026-10-10). No per-cartridge licence files.
- Lineage: `project.attribution.lineage[]` required (empty = original work).
- i18n: every label object carries `en`, `es`, `fr`, `pt`.
- Interfaces: `spine`/`gutter`, `glue_flap` ↔ `glue_zone`, `tab` ↔ `slot`, `hinge`, `page_edge`,
  `pivot` (matched to a Yantra4D brad through `hardware_ref`), `track`.

## Classes (the launch ladder)

1. Techniques (page turn, folds, reverse folds, squash, petal, rabbit ear, pleat, tab-and-slot,
   glue flap, score, perforation). 2. Bases. 3. Traditional models (attributed to tradition).
4. Tessellations and engineering origami. 5. Kirigami. 6. Papercut traditions (community credit).
7. Paper engineering (pop-up mechanisms). 8. Book structures. 9. Flexagons and toys.
10. Dioramas (compositions through interfaces).

## Heritage and provenance

Traditional models cite sources and are credited to their tradition; papercut traditions credit
their communities (papel picado: San Salvador Huixcolotla, Puebla; amate: the Otomí of San Pablito,
Pahuatlán, Puebla). Modern designers' crease patterns are copyrighted and never used.

## Process

One agent per slug; the coordinator alone writes indexes and only when landing a passing cartridge;
the coordinator moves Pliego's pin to this repository after these lanes are green. Third-party
contributions wait on the CLA-vs-DCO ruling.

## CI

GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`, actions pinned by SHA, `contents: read`. Lanes: triple, manifests
(`pliego-spec` at `SPEC_PIN`), render (`pliego-kernel` at `PLIEGO_PIN`), byte and file-size gates.
An unset pin prints `skip: <PIN> not set`.
